overall: The AG found two violations: an insufficiently specific executive session purpose in the Sept. 21, 2017 notice (technical) and counsel responding to a complaint without a Commission meeting to review it. The 48-hour posting, topic detail, and procedure claims were rejected.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to post notice of its Sept. 21, 2017 meeting at least 48 hours in advance, citing a website date stamp showing the meeting day.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Commission posted the notice more than 48 hours prior to the September 21, 2017 meeting, notwithstanding the errant posting date listed on the website.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the meeting notice gave insufficient detail about each executive session topic.
allegations.key_passage: On the facts present here, we find that the Commission permissibly withheld identifying information about each individual or topic discussed during the September 21, 2017 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the notice did not identify which statutory purpose justified the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this failure constituted a technical violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission entered executive session without following proper procedure.
allegations.key_passage: Our review of the meeting minutes shows that the Commission followed all required procedural steps.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged counsel responded to an Open Meeting Law complaint without the Commission first meeting to review it.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to meet to review the first Open Meeting Law complaint addressed in this letter prior to the response from counsel.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
